what_its_for: Daridorexant is used to help adults who have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep (a condition called insomnia). It works by blocking certain signals in your brain that keep you awake, helping your body naturally fall asleep.
how_to_take: Take daridorexant by mouth as a tablet. Swallow it whole with or without food. Take it only when you are ready to go to bed and have at least 7 hours before you need to wake up. Do not take it if you cannot get a full night of sleep.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 25 mg taken once per night, right before bedtime. Your doctor may increase your dose to 50 mg if needed. Never take more than one dose per night. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: Daridorexant is taken only when needed at bedtime, so a traditional missed dose does not apply. If you go to bed and forget to take it, only take it if you still have at least 7 hours left before you need to wake up. Never double up or take two doses in one night.
storage: Store daridorexant at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking daridorexant, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness and raise the risk of serious side effects. Do not drive a car, operate heavy machinery, or do any activity that requires you to be fully alert the morning after taking this medication, as you may still feel drowsy. Avoid taking other sleep aids, sedatives, or medicines that cause drowsiness unless your doctor approves. Avoid eating a large, high-fat meal right before taking it, as this may slow how quickly the medication works.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: unusual behaviors during sleep such as sleepwalking, sleep-driving, or doing other activities while not fully awake; feelings of depression, thoughts of self-harm, or worsening mood; severe next-day drowsiness that affects your ability to function; temporary inability to move or speak when waking up or falling asleep (sleep paralysis); or seeing, hearing, or feeling things that are not there (hallucinations). Also contact your doctor if your sleep problems do not improve after a few weeks.
when_it_works: Daridorexant begins working within 30 minutes of taking it. You should take it only when you are in bed and ready to sleep. You may notice improvement in your ability to fall asleep and stay asleep within the first few nights, but it may take 1 to 2 weeks to see the full benefit.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and older): You may be more sensitive to the effects of this medication, including dizziness and falls. Use caution and talk to your doctor about the right dose for you. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of this medication during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully established. Liver problems: If you have moderate liver disease, your doctor will likely lower your dose. This medication is not recommended if you have severe liver disease. Kidney problems: No dose adjustment is usually needed for kidney problems, but talk to your doctor. Children: This medication is not approved for use in anyone under 18 years of age.
